Unforgettable Experiences by Local Guides

Passion • Honesty • Professionalism • Trustworthiness

Discover Italy, a country renowned for possessing more than half of the world's artistic treasures and embodying cultural richness that transcends the tangible. Our dedicated team of Italians reveals the lesser-known, serene corners of Tuscany, steering clear of bustling tourist hubs and unveiling hidden gems accessible only to locals. With an intimate understanding and access to Tuscany's most exquisite locales, we promise our guests a mesmerizing encounter with ancient monasteries, centuries-old castles, storied fortresses, historical residences and estates, local museums, archaeological sites, and UNESCO heritage sites.

Our website primarily caters to American visitors seeking luxury villas and rental villas in Tuscany for an exclusive, authentic, and unique vacation experience. Let us help you craft a truly luxurious and unforgettable stay in Tuscany, where every detail is tailored to your desires.

pages.mainHtml:
A Meal with an Italian Family

Having a meal with an Italian family in Tuscany is a heartwarming experience. You'll be welcomed into a cozy atmosphere, treated to generous portions of home-cooked dishes using local ingredients. The meal, typically featuring multiple courses and local wines, is a celebration of family, friendship, and cultural exchange. Expect lively conversations, laughter, and a genuine sense of joy throughout the dining experience, concluding with gratitude and fond farewells.

pages.title: About
pages.mainHtml:
About

Passion • Honesty •
Professionalism • Trustworthiness

Super Tuscany is the brainchild of Christian Ferrara, an impassioned Italian living in America, who desires to share the passion, the zeal, and the intoxicating allure of his homeland, Tuscany, Italy. What he envisions is not just a vacation but a journey—an adventure that beckons you to immerse yourself in the timeless embrace of Tuscany's culture, unfolding the classic "la dolce vita" experience, where every moment echoes the rhythms of local Italian life.

Meet Christian Ferrara, a 47-year-old entrepreneur, a native son of Italy who transplanted himself to the hustle and bustle of New York a decade ago. His roots in hospitality sprouted from an innate love for food and wine, and the joy of sharing these pleasures with others. In 2019, after becoming an American citizen and building an impressive career, he found himself at a crossroads. While tempting offers to explore new horizons beckoned, his heart remained steadfast in the area of hospitality, leading him to the creation of his own company.

Working with many customers, through the hospitality industry, Christian would often be asked for recommendations, advice, and to be told stories about Italy. During these conversations, his guests confessed they desired to travel to the region and get to have a more authentic experience, such as he spoke about. They craved authenticity—to witness the wonders with their own eyes, to absorb the essence of Tuscan culture, to wander through the living tapestry of art and architecture, to traverse hills painted in postcard-perfect hues, and to savor the local wines, essentially, to live life as a local Italian.

Hence, Super Tuscany was born. During a recent visit to Italy, he shared the concept of his project with all his hometown friends. All born and raised in Italy, now all professionals in different industries, such as wines and food, hospitality,and tourism, they form a group of 25 friends. United by a shared passion, culture, and vision, they form an artistic ensemble, collaborating to craft an experience tailored for you.

Our recipe is elegantly simple, yet potent—infused with passion, honesty, professionalism, trustworthiness, and an authentic love for people and hospitality. When you embark on this journey with us, you're not just a customer; you become a cherished friend for life.

pages.title: Accessibility Statement
pages.mainHtml:
Accessibility Statement

Supertuscany.org is committed to providing a website that is accessible to the widest possible audience, regardless of circumstances and abilities. We aim to adhere as closely as possible to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.0, Level AA), published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible to people with disabilities. Adhering to these guidelines will help make the web more user-friendly for everyone. Supertuscany.org is dedicated to complying with the guidelines and standards for accessibility. However, it is not always possible to do so in all areas of our website, and we are continuously working towards achieving this goal. Due to the dynamic nature of a website, minor issues may occasionally occur during periodic updates. We are constantly seeking solutions to bring all areas of the site to the same level of overall web accessibility. If you have any comments and/or suggestions on how we can improve the accessibility of our website, please do not hesitate to contact our Accessibility Coordinator by phone at +1 (917) 724-3124 or via email at info@supertuscany.org. Your feedback will help us enhance our website.

Bike Tours

Tuscany's bike tours offer a scenic and cultural adventure through rolling hills and charming villages. With routes catering to various skill levels, cyclists can explore vineyards, olive groves, and historic towns. Guided or self-guided options provide flexibility, and tours often include culinary experiences like wine tastings. It's an eco-friendly way to soak in Tuscany's beauty and rich heritage.

pages.title: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
pages.mainHtml:
Bistecca alla Fiorentina

"Bistecca alla Fiorentina" is a renowned Tuscan dish that showcases the region's commitment to simple yet high-quality cuisine. This traditional Florentine-style steak is a Tuscany culinary icon, known for its distinct preparation and robust flavors.

Key features of Bistecca alla Fiorentina:

  1. Cut: The steak used is typically a thick-cut T-bone or porterhouse, ensuring a generous portion of both tenderloin and sirloin.

  2. Grilling: The steak is seasoned with salt and sometimes olive oil, then grilled over an open flame or hot coals. The grilling process imparts a delicious smokiness to the meat.

  3. Rare to Medium-Rare: Bistecca alla Fiorentina is traditionally served rare to medium-rare, allowing the natural flavors of the beef to shine. The inside remains tender and juicy.

  4. Size: The size of the steak is substantial, often meant for sharing. It reflects the Tuscan preference for simplicity and emphasizing the quality of the meat.

pages.title: Chestnut Harvest
pages.mainHtml:
Chestnut Harvest

The chestnut harvest in Tuscany, from late September to November, is a festive season marked by community gatherings and culinary delights. People venture into forests to collect chestnuts, and towns host festivals featuring roasted chestnuts and traditional activities. The harvest not only provides a bounty of nuts but also offers a chance to celebrate the region's rich cultural and culinary heritage.

pages.mainHtml:
Cookie Policy of www.supertuscany.org

To find more information on California consumers and their privacy rights, Users may read the privacy policy.

To find more information on Virginia consumers and their privacy rights, Users may read the privacy policy.

To find more information on Colorado consumers and their privacy rights, Users may read the privacy policy.

To find more information on Connecticut consumers and their privacy rights, Users may read the privacy policy.

To find more information on Utah consumers and their privacy rights, Users may read the privacy policy.

This document informs Users about the technologies that help www.supertuscany.org to achieve the purposes described below. Such technologies allow the Owner to access and store information (for example by using a Cookie) or use resources (for example by running a script) on a User’s device as they interact with www.supertuscany.org.

For simplicity, all such technologies are defined as "Trackers" within this document – unless there is a reason to differentiate.
For example, while Cookies can be used on both web and mobile browsers, it would be inaccurate to talk about Cookies in the context of mobile apps as they are a browser-based Tracker. For this reason, within this document, the term Cookies is only used where it is specifically meant to indicate that particular type of Tracker.

Some of the purposes for which Trackers are used may also require the User's consent. Whenever consent is given, it can be freely withdrawn at any time following the instructions provided in this document.

Www.supertuscany.org uses Trackers managed directly by the Owner (so-called “first-party” Trackers) and Trackers that enable services provided by a third-party (so-called “third-party” Trackers). Unless otherwise specified within this document, third-party providers may access the Trackers managed by them.
The validity and expiration periods of Cookies and other similar Trackers may vary depending on the lifetime set by the Owner or the relevant provider. Some of them expire upon termination of the User’s browsing session.
In addition to what’s specified in the descriptions within each of the categories below, Users may find more precise and updated information regarding lifetime specification as well as any other relevant information — such as the presence of other Trackers — in the linked privacy policies of the respective third-party providers or by contacting the Owner.

Activities strictly necessary for the operation of www.supertuscany.org and delivery of the Service

Www.supertuscany.org uses so-called “technical” Cookies and other similar Trackers to carry out activities that are strictly necessary for the operation or delivery of the Service.

Third-party Trackers

  • Platform services and hosting

    These services have the purpose of hosting and running key components of www.supertuscany.org, therefore allowing the provision of www.supertuscany.org from within a unified platform. Such platforms provide a wide range of tools to the Owner – e.g. analytics, user registration, commenting, database management, e-commerce, payment processing – that imply the collection and handling of Personal Data.
    Some of these services work through geographically distributed servers, making it difficult to determine the actual location where the Personal Data are stored.

    Wix (Wix.com, Ltd.)

    Wix is a platform provided by Wix.com, Ltd. that allows the Owner to build, run and host www.supertuscany.org.
    Wix is highly customizable and can host websites from simple blogs to complex e-commerce platforms.

    Personal Data processed: billing address, device information, email address, first name, last name, payment info, phone number, shipping address, Trackers and Usage Data.

    Place of processing: Israel – Privacy Policy.

    Storage duration:

    • XSRF-TOKEN: duration of the session

    • _wixCIDX: 3 months

    • _wix_browser_sess: duration of the session

    • bSession: 30 minutes

    • hs: duration of the session

    • ssr-caching: duration of the session

    • svSession: 1 year

Other activities involving the use of Trackers

Functionality

Www.supertuscany.org uses Trackers to enable basic interactions and functionalities, allowing Users to access selected features of the Service and facilitating the User's communication with the Owner.

  • Contacting the User

    Contact form (www.supertuscany.org)

    By filling in the contact form with their Data, the User authorizes www.supertuscany.org to use these details to reply to requests for information, quotes or any other kind of request as indicated by the form’s header.

    Personal Data processed: email address, first name, last name, phone number, Trackers and various types of Data.

Measurement

Www.supertuscany.org uses Trackers to measure traffic and analyze User behavior to improve the Service.

  • Analytics

    The services contained in this section enable the Owner to monitor and analyze web traffic and can be used to keep track of User behavior.

    Google Analytics 4 (Google LLC)

    Google Analytics 4 is a web analysis service provided by Google LLC (“Google”). Google utilizes the Data collected to track and examine the use of www.supertuscany.org, to prepare reports on its activities and share them with other Google services.
    Google may use the Data collected to contextualize and personalize the ads of its own advertising network.
    In Google Analytics 4, IP addresses are used at collection time and then discarded before Data is logged in any data center or server. Users can learn more by consulting Google’s official documentation.

    In order to understand Google's use of Data, consult Google's partner policy.

    Personal Data processed: number of Users, session statistics, Trackers and Usage Data.

    Place of processing: United States – Privacy Policy – Opt Out.

    Storage duration:

    • _ga: 2 years

    • _ga_*: 2 years

How to manage preferences and provide or withdraw consent

There are various ways to manage Tracker related preferences and to provide and withdraw consent, where relevant:

Users can manage preferences related to Trackers from directly within their own device settings, for example, by preventing the use or storage of Trackers.

Additionally, whenever the use of Trackers is based on consent, Users can provide or withdraw such consent by setting their preferences within the cookie notice or by updating such preferences accordingly via the relevant consent-preferences privacy widget, if available.

It is also possible, via relevant browser or device features, to delete previously stored Trackers, including those used to remember the User’s initial consent preferences.

Other Trackers in the browser’s local memory may be cleared by deleting the browsing history.

With regard to any third-party Trackers, Users can manage their preferences via the related opt-out link (where provided), by using the means indicated in the third party's privacy policy, or by contacting the third party.

Locating Tracker Settings

Users can, for example, find information about how to manage Cookies in the most commonly used browsers at the following addresses:

  • Google Chrome

  • Mozilla Firefox

  • Apple Safari

  • Microsoft Internet Explorer

  • Microsoft Edge

  • Brave

  • Opera

Users may also manage certain categories of Trackers used on mobile apps by opting out through relevant device settings such as the device advertising settings for mobile devices, or tracking settings in general (Users may open the device settings and look for the relevant setting).

Consequences of denying the use of Trackers

Users are free to decide whether or not to allow the use of Trackers. However, please note that Trackers help www.supertuscany.org to provide a better experience and advanced functionalities to Users (in line with the purposes outlined in this document). Therefore, if the User chooses to block the use of Trackers, the Owner may be unable to provide related features.

Owner and Data Controller

Supertuscany LLC di Christian Ferrara
885 Grand Street - 11211 Brooklyn NY

Owner contact email: info@supertuscany.org

Since the use of third-party Trackers through www.supertuscany.org cannot be fully controlled by the Owner, any specific references to third-party Trackers are to be considered indicative. In order to obtain complete information, Users are kindly requested to consult the privacy policies of the respective third-party services listed in this document.

Given the objective complexity surrounding tracking technologies, Users are encouraged to contact the Owner should they wish to receive any further information on the use of such technologies by www.supertuscany.org.

Definitions and legal references

Personal Data (or Data)

Any information that directly, indirectly, or in connection with other information — including a personal identification number — allows for the identification or identifiability of a natural person.

Usage Data

Information collected automatically through www.supertuscany.org (or third-party services employed in www.supertuscany.org), which can include: the IP addresses or domain names of the computers utilized by the Users who use www.supertuscany.org, the URI addresses (Uniform Resource Identifier), the time of the request, the method utilized to submit the request to the server, the size of the file received in response, the numerical code indicating the status of the server's answer (successful outcome, error, etc.), the country of origin, the features of the browser and the operating system utilized by the User, the various time details per visit (e.g., the time spent on each page within the Application) and the details about the path followed within the Application with special reference to the sequence of pages visited, and other parameters about the device operating system and/or the User's IT environment.

User

The individual using www.supertuscany.org who, unless otherwise specified, coincides with the Data Subject.

Data Subject

The natural person to whom the Personal Data refers.

Data Processor (or Processor)

The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller, as described in this privacy policy.

Data Controller (or Owner)

The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of Personal Data, including the security measures concerning the operation and use of www.supertuscany.org. The Data Controller, unless otherwise specified, is the Owner of www.supertuscany.org.

www.supertuscany.org (or this Application)

The means by which the Personal Data of the User is collected and processed.

Service

The service provided by www.supertuscany.org as described in the relative terms (if available) and on this site/application.

European Union (or EU)

Unless otherwise specified, all references made within this document to the European Union include all current member states to the European Union and the European Economic Area.

Cookie

Cookies are Trackers consisting of small sets of data stored in the User's browser.

Tracker

Tracker indicates any technology - e.g Cookies, unique identifiers, web beacons, embedded scripts, e-tags and fingerprinting - that enables the tracking of Users, for example by accessing or storing information on the User’s device.

Legal information

This privacy statement has been prepared based on provisions of multiple legislations.

This privacy policy relates solely to www.supertuscany.org, if not stated otherwise within this document.

pages.title: Cooking Classes
pages.mainHtml:
Cooking Classes

Tuscan cooking classes are immersive experiences where participants learn to prepare traditional dishes with fresh, local ingredients. Led by skilled chefs, these hands-on classes cover iconic recipes, culinary tips, and may include wine pairing. Set in picturesque locations, the classes often end with a shared meal, fostering a sense of community and leaving participants with lasting memories of Tuscan gastronomy.

Italian Local Guides can be available at your request. Contact us for details and pricing.

pages.title: Tuscany Museums
pages.mainHtml:
Tuscany Museums

Tuscany's museums showcase a wealth of artistic and historical treasures:

  1. Uffizi Gallery: Home to Renaissance masterpieces in Florence.

  2. Accademia Gallery: Houses Michelangelo's David and other Renaissance art.

  3. Pitti Palace: A vast complex in Florence featuring multiple museums.

  4. Museo dell'Opera del Duomo: Displays sculptures and art from Florence's cathedral complex.

  5. Museo Galileo: Dedicated to the history of science in Florence.

  6. Museo Nazionale del Bargello: Exhibits Renaissance sculptures in Florence.

  7. National Archaeological Museum of Florence: Showcases Etruscan, Roman, and Egyptian artifacts.

  8. Museum of San Salvi: Features religious art in Florence.

  9. Pinacoteca di Siena: Displays Sienese paintings in Siena.

  10. Leonardo da Vinci Museum: Located in Vinci, dedicated to da Vinci's life and inventions.

Each museum offers a unique glimpse into Tuscany's cultural and artistic heritage.

pages.mainHtml:
Nature

Price

From $600 (it depends on the activities requested)

Duration

Flexible (minimum 2 people)

Embark on a mesmerizing journey as you traverse the enchanting trails of Tuscany, guided by a certified Italian expert well-versed in the region's history. This full-day adventure is meticulously curated, providing immersive insights into the tales behind towns, castles, sanctuaries, and the scenic routes that unfold before you.

Throughout the day, moments of serenity are punctuated with pleasant breaks beneath centuries-old oak trees, where you can relish the experience of indulging in an authentic Italian panino. To elevate your nature hiking expedition, consider a distinctive interlude with an unforgettable horseback riding experience led by an Italian riding instructor. Immerse yourself in the breathtaking views that the hills and forests of Tuscany graciously present.

We know every single corner of our beautiful Tuscany and we can customize your trail lenght based your personal training's level and your willing to explore our fascinating land.

Included on the price: Italian snack/panino with some refreshments and a lunch in any of the popular restaurant along the way (3 courses lunch with a glass of wine)

Private professioanl Italian guide

Trasportation

Arezzo

A Brief History

Arezzo is a city in Tuscany, Italy, with a rich history that dates back to ancient times. Here is a brief overview of its history:

  • Ancient origins: Arezzo has ancient origins, believed to have been initially settled by the Etruscans. It later became a Roman colony known as Arretium during the Roman Republic.

  • Medieval era: During the Middle Ages, Arezzo was an important city-state and a significant cultural and economic center in Tuscany. It was known for its thriving artistic and intellectual community, which included renowned figures such as the poet Petrarch.

  • Renaissance period: Arezzo flourished during the Renaissance, particularly in the 14th and 15th centuries. It became a hub for artistic and architectural developments, with notable artists and architects contributing to the city's cultural heritage.

  • Incorporation into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany: Arezzo was later incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in the 16th century and remained a part of it until the unification of Italy in the 19th century.

  • Modern era: Following Italian unification in the 19th century, Arezzo became a part of the Kingdom of Italy. The city has since evolved into a modern urban center while preserving its rich historical and cultural legacy.

Today, Arezzo is known for its well-preserved medieval and Renaissance architecture, including churches, palaces, and public squares. The city is also recognized for its artistic heritage and its historical significance in the development of Tuscan culture. It continues to attract visitors from around the world who come to explore its historical landmarks, museums, and cultural events, as well as to experience the beauty and charm of Tuscany.

Experiences

Arezzo, Italy, offers a variety of attractions and activities for visitors to enjoy. Here are some of the top things to do in Arezzo:

  1. Explore the historic city center: Wander through the charming streets of the historic city center, where you can admire the well-preserved medieval and Renaissance architecture, including the Piazza Grande, the Cathedral of Arezzo, and the Basilica of San Francesco.

  2. Visit historical landmarks: Explore significant historical landmarks, such as the Medici Fortress, the Roman amphitheater, and the Church of San Domenico, which houses the famous Cimabue's crucifix.

  3. Discover cultural treasures: Explore the city's cultural heritage by visiting museums such as the Museo Casa Vasari, dedicated to the life and works of the renowned artist Giorgio Vasari, and the State Museum of Medieval and Modern Art, featuring a collection of paintings and sculptures.

  4. Attend local events and festivals: Experience the vibrant local culture by participating in events and festivals, including the Giostra del Saracino, a traditional medieval jousting tournament held twice a year, and the Arezzo Antique Fair, one of the most important antique fairs in Italy.

  5. Sample local cuisine: Indulge in Tuscan cuisine at the local trattorias and restaurants, where you can savor traditional dishes such as bistecca alla fiorentina (Florentine steak), ribollita, and pici pasta, accompanied by locally produced wines such as Chianti and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.

  6. Enjoy the surrounding countryside: Take a day trip to explore the picturesque Tuscan countryside surrounding Arezzo, with its rolling hills, vineyards, and olive groves. You can also visit nearby towns and villages, including Cortona and Montepulciano, known for their beauty and historical significance.

  7. Attend cultural performances: Enjoy cultural performances, including concerts, theatrical productions, and other artistic events, often hosted at various venues throughout the city, showcasing local and international talent.

These activities provide a glimpse of the diverse cultural, historical, and culinary experiences that Arezzo has to offer, making it an enticing destination for travelers interested in exploring the rich heritage and natural beauty of Tuscany.

Arezzo is a city in Tuscany, Italy, with a rich history that dates back to ancient times. Here is a brief overview of its history:

  • Ancient origins: Arezzo has ancient origins, believed to have been initially settled by the Etruscans. It later became a Roman colony known as Arretium during the Roman Republic.

  • Medieval era: During the Middle Ages, Arezzo was an important city-state and a significant cultural and economic center in Tuscany. It was known for its thriving artistic and intellectual community, which included renowned figures such as the poet Petrarch.

  • Renaissance period: Arezzo flourished during the Renaissance, particularly in the 14th and 15th centuries. It became a hub for artistic and architectural developments, with notable artists and architects contributing to the city's cultural heritage.

  • Incorporation into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany: Arezzo was later incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in the 16th century and remained a part of it until the unification of Italy in the 19th century.

  • Modern era: Following Italian unification in the 19th century, Arezzo became a part of the Kingdom of Italy. The city has since evolved into a modern urban center while preserving its rich historical and cultural legacy.

Today, Arezzo is known for its well-preserved medieval and Renaissance architecture, including churches, palaces, and public squares. The city is also recognized for its artistic heritage and its historical significance in the development of Tuscan culture. It continues to attract visitors from around the world who come to explore its historical landmarks, museums, and cultural events, as well as to experience the beauty and charm of Tuscany.

sections.heading: Experiences
sections.html:
Arezzo, Italy, offers a variety of attractions and activities for visitors to enjoy. Here are some of the top things to do in Arezzo:

  1. Explore the historic city center: Wander through the charming streets of the historic city center, where you can admire the well-preserved medieval and Renaissance architecture, including the Piazza Grande, the Cathedral of Arezzo, and the Basilica of San Francesco.

  2. Visit historical landmarks: Explore significant historical landmarks, such as the Medici Fortress, the Roman amphitheater, and the Church of San Domenico, which houses the famous Cimabue's crucifix.

  3. Discover cultural treasures: Explore the city's cultural heritage by visiting museums such as the Museo Casa Vasari, dedicated to the life and works of the renowned artist Giorgio Vasari, and the State Museum of Medieval and Modern Art, featuring a collection of paintings and sculptures.

  4. Attend local events and festivals: Experience the vibrant local culture by participating in events and festivals, including the Giostra del Saracino, a traditional medieval jousting tournament held twice a year, and the Arezzo Antique Fair, one of the most important antique fairs in Italy.

  5. Sample local cuisine: Indulge in Tuscan cuisine at the local trattorias and restaurants, where you can savor traditional dishes such as bistecca alla fiorentina (Florentine steak), ribollita, and pici pasta, accompanied by locally produced wines such as Chianti and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.

  6. Enjoy the surrounding countryside: Take a day trip to explore the picturesque Tuscan countryside surrounding Arezzo, with its rolling hills, vineyards, and olive groves. You can also visit nearby towns and villages, including Cortona and Montepulciano, known for their beauty and historical significance.

  7. Attend cultural performances: Enjoy cultural performances, including concerts, theatrical productions, and other artistic events, often hosted at various venues throughout the city, showcasing local and international talent.

These activities provide a glimpse of the diverse cultural, historical, and culinary experiences that Arezzo has to offer, making it an enticing destination for travelers interested in exploring the rich heritage and natural beauty of Tuscany.

Firenze

A Brief History

Florence, or Firenze in Italian, is a city located in the Tuscany region of Italy and is renowned for its rich history, cultural significance, and artistic heritage. Here is a concise overview of its history:

  • Ancient and Medieval Times: Florence's history dates back to Roman times when it was established as a settlement during the 1st century BCE. However, its real ascent to prominence occurred during the Middle Ages when it became a thriving center for trade and finance. It eventually evolved into a city-state and, in the 14th century, became a significant cultural and economic powerhouse in Europe.

  • Renaissance Golden Age: Florence reached the peak of its cultural and artistic significance during the Renaissance, particularly in the 15th and 16th centuries. The city became a vibrant hub of creativity, fostering the talents of renowned artists and intellectuals such as Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Botticelli. Prominent families such as the Medici played a crucial role in patronizing the arts and contributing to Florence's cultural legacy.

  • Political Turbulence: Despite its cultural accomplishments, Florence experienced political upheavals and power struggles, leading to periods of instability. Conflict between powerful families and city-states in Italy, such as the ongoing rivalry with Pisa and other neighboring regions, often shaped Florence's political landscape.

  • Unification of Italy: During the 19th century, Florence became an integral part of the process of Italian unification, which culminated in the establishment of the Kingdom of Italy in 1861. The city served as the capital of the Kingdom from 1865 to 1871.

  • Modern Era: In the 20th century, Florence continued to thrive as a center for art, culture, and tourism. Its historic center, with landmarks such as the Florence Cathedral (Duomo), the Uffizi Gallery, and the Ponte Vecchio, attracts millions of tourists each year, cementing its position as one of Italy's most significant cultural destinations.

Today, Florence remains a prominent cultural hub, renowned for its artistic treasures, architectural marvels, and vibrant cultural scene, making it a must-visit destination for travelers from around the world.

Experiences

Firenze, the capital of Italy's Tuscany region, is renowned for its rich history, cultural heritage, and remarkable art and architecture. Here are some of the top things to do in Florence:

  1. Visit the Duomo: Explore the iconic Florence Cathedral (Duomo) with its breathtaking architecture, including Brunelleschi's Dome, Giotto's Bell Tower, and the Baptistery of St. John.

  2. Admire Art at the Uffizi Gallery: Discover masterpieces by renowned artists such as Botticelli, Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, and Raphael at the world-famous Uffizi Gallery, one of the most prominent art museums in the world.

  3. Explore the Galleria dell'Accademia: Marvel at Michelangelo's famous sculpture of David and other works of art at the Galleria dell'Accademia.

  4. Walk across the Ponte Vecchio: Enjoy the picturesque views while strolling across the historic Ponte Vecchio, a medieval stone bridge lined with shops, art dealers, and jewelers.

  5. Discover Palazzo Vecchio: Visit the Palazzo Vecchio, Florence's town hall, to admire its impressive architecture and explore the significant art and history it houses.

  6. Wander through the Boboli Gardens: Spend time at the Boboli Gardens, located behind the Pitti Palace, and enjoy the beauty of this historic park filled with sculptures, fountains, and stunning greenery.

  7. Visit the Pitti Palace: Explore the Pitti Palace, a vast Renaissance palace that houses several museums and galleries, including the Palatine Gallery, the Royal Apartments, and the Gallery of Modern Art.

  8. Discover the Basilica of Santa Croce: Visit the Basilica of Santa Croce, the principal Franciscan church in Florence, known for its stunning architecture and being the burial place of many notable Italians, including Michelangelo, Galileo, and Machiavelli.

  9. Stroll through Piazza della Signoria: Experience the lively atmosphere of Piazza della Signoria, one of Florence's main squares, surrounded by impressive sculptures and historic buildings, including the Palazzo Vecchio.

  10. Indulge in Tuscan Cuisine: Enjoy authentic Tuscan cuisine at the city's many restaurants, trattorias, and cafes, sampling local specialties such as Florentine steak, ribollita, and pappa al pomodoro, along with a variety of renowned Tuscan wines.

Florence offers a multitude of cultural, historical, and culinary experiences that make it a must-visit destination for travelers seeking to immerse themselves in the art and history of Italy.

Grosseto

A Brief History

Grosseto is a historic city located in the Tuscany region of Italy, known for its cultural heritage, natural beauty, and ancient origins. Here is a concise overview of its history:

  • Ancient Times: The area around Grosseto has a history dating back to ancient times, with evidence of Etruscan and Roman settlements. The city itself is believed to have been founded during the High Middle Ages.

  • Medieval Period: Grosseto played a significant role in the medieval history of Tuscany, serving as an important strategic stronghold for various ruling powers, including the Aldobrandeschi and the Medici families.

  • Renaissance and Modern Era: During the Renaissance, Grosseto experienced periods of cultural and economic growth under the patronage of the Medici family, contributing to the city's artistic and architectural heritage.

  • 19th and 20th Centuries: Like many other regions in Italy, Grosseto was part of the Italian unification process in the 19th century, eventually becoming part of the Kingdom of Italy in 1861.

  • Contemporary Period: In recent times, Grosseto has emerged as a popular destination for tourists seeking to explore the beauty of the Tuscan countryside and experience the rich cultural offerings of the region. The city has maintained its historical charm while embracing modern developments, catering to both locals and visitors with its cultural events, local cuisine, and natural attractions.

Today, Grosseto continues to attract travelers with its picturesque landscapes, historic architecture, and cultural events, making it a captivating destination for those interested in experiencing the rich history and natural beauty of Tuscany.

Experiences

Grosseto, located in the picturesque Tuscany region of Italy, offers a range of activities for visitors to enjoy. Here are some of the things you can do in and around Grosseto:

  1. Visit the Medicean Walls: Explore the well-preserved Medicean Walls that once surrounded the city. These historic fortifications offer a glimpse into Grosseto's past and provide panoramic views of the surrounding area.

  2. Explore the Cathedral of San Lorenzo: Visit the Cathedral of San Lorenzo, an impressive medieval cathedral located in the heart of Grosseto. Admire its architecture, artwork, and historical significance.

  3. Discover the Archaeological Museum: Learn about the ancient history of the region by visiting the Archaeological Museum of Grosseto, which houses a collection of Etruscan and Roman artifacts.

  4. Relax on the Beaches: Enjoy the beautiful beaches along the Maremma coastline, such as Marina di Grosseto and Castiglione della Pescaia, which offer opportunities for sunbathing, swimming, and water sports.

  5. Explore the Maremma Natural Park: Discover the natural beauty of the Maremma Natural Park, a protected area known for its diverse wildlife, hiking trails, and scenic landscapes. Enjoy activities such as birdwatching, hiking, and nature photography.

  6. Taste Local Cuisine: Indulge in the local Tuscan cuisine by visiting traditional restaurants and trattorias in Grosseto. Sample regional dishes such as pici pasta, wild boar stew, and other specialties made with locally sourced ingredients.

  7. Wine Tasting in the Maremma Region: Take a wine tour in the Maremma wine region, known for its excellent wines, including Morellino di Scansano and Vermentino. Visit local wineries to taste and learn about the production of these renowned Tuscan wines.

  8. Visit nearby towns and villages: Take day trips to nearby towns and villages, such as Pitigliano, Sorano, and Sovana, which offer historical sites, charming streets, and cultural attractions that reflect the region's rich history and heritage.

Grosseto and its surrounding areas provide a perfect blend of history, natural beauty, and culinary delights, offering visitors a memorable and authentic Tuscan experience.

Lucca

A Brief History

Lucca is a city in Tuscany, Italy, with a rich history that dates back to ancient times. Here is a brief overview of its history:

  • Ancient origins: Lucca was originally founded by the Etruscans and later became a Roman colony in 180 BC. Under the Roman Empire, it prospered as an important city along the Via Cassia, an ancient Roman road.

  • Medieval era: During the Middle Ages, Lucca flourished as an independent city-state and a prosperous trading center along the Silk Road. It became a significant political and economic power in Tuscany, and its strategic location contributed to its wealth and influence.

  • Renaissance period: In the 14th century, Lucca came under the rule of the powerful Guinigi family, who transformed the city with notable architectural and artistic contributions. The city became a hub for cultural and artistic developments during the Renaissance.

  • Incorporation into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany: Lucca was later incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in the 16th century and remained a part of it until the unification of Italy in the 19th century.

  • Modern era: Following Italian unification in the 19th century, Lucca became a part of the Kingdom of Italy. Despite its incorporation into the unified Italian state, Lucca has managed to preserve its historic charm and architectural heritage, attracting tourists and travelers from around the world.

Today, Lucca is renowned for its well-preserved Renaissance walls, which encircle the historic city center, as well as its impressive medieval and Renaissance architecture, including churches, towers, and palaces. The city continues to be a vibrant cultural hub, known for its cultural events, music festivals, and picturesque landscapes, making it a popular destination for tourists seeking to explore Tuscany's rich history and heritage.

Experiences

Lucca, Italy, offers a rich array of attractions and activities for visitors to enjoy. Here are some of the top things to do in Lucca:

  1. Walk or bike the Renaissance walls: Lucca is famous for its well-preserved Renaissance walls, which encircle the historic city center. You can rent a bike or take a leisurely stroll along the tree-lined paths on top of the walls, offering picturesque views of the city and its surroundings.

  2. Explore the historic city center: Wander through the narrow streets of the city center to discover Lucca's charming squares, ancient churches, and historic buildings. Visit the Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, which was once a Roman amphitheater and is now a bustling square lined with cafes and shops.

  3. Visit historical landmarks: Explore the city's architectural gems, such as the Lucca Cathedral (Duomo di Lucca), the Basilica of San Frediano, and the Guinigi Tower, known for its rooftop garden with oak trees.

  4. Enjoy cultural events and festivals: Lucca hosts various cultural events and festivals throughout the year, including the Lucca Summer Festival, which features concerts by renowned international artists, as well as the Lucca Comics & Games festival, one of the largest comic book and gaming events in Europe.

  5. Sample local cuisine: Indulge in traditional Tuscan cuisine at the local trattorias and restaurants, offering dishes such as ribollita, pappa al pomodoro, and other regional specialties. Don't forget to taste the local wines, such as the famous Tuscan reds.

  6. Relax in the parks and gardens: Spend some time in Lucca's peaceful parks and gardens, such as the Botanical Gardens of Lucca or the Palazzo Pfanner gardens, known for their beauty and tranquility.

  7. Attend musical events: Lucca is known for its rich musical heritage, so try to catch a classical music concert or opera performance at one of the city's historic venues, such as the Teatro del Giglio.

  8. Take day trips to nearby attractions: Use Lucca as a base to explore other nearby attractions in Tuscany, including Pisa, Florence, and the picturesque Tuscan countryside.

These activities offer just a glimpse of the many attractions and experiences that Lucca has to offer, making it a delightful destination for travelers interested in history, culture, and the beauty of Tuscany.

Pisa

A Brief History

Pisa, located in the Tuscany region of Italy, has a rich history that dates back to ancient times. Here is a brief overview of its history:

  • Ancient and Medieval Times: Pisa's history can be traced back to the time of the Etruscans, an ancient Italian civilization. During the Middle Ages, Pisa emerged as a powerful maritime republic, competing with other Italian city-states like Genoa and Venice for dominance in trade and commerce. The city played a significant role in the maritime expansion of the Mediterranean region, establishing colonies and trading posts along the coasts of Italy and beyond.

  • Golden Age and Cultural Flourishing: Pisa's Golden Age occurred during the 11th and 12th centuries, characterized by economic prosperity, architectural achievements, and cultural flourishing. This period saw the construction of some of Pisa's most iconic landmarks, including the famous Leaning Tower, the Cathedral (Duomo), and the Baptistry, all located within the Piazza dei Miracoli (Square of Miracles).

  • Struggles and Decline: Pisa faced various struggles and conflicts, including clashes with other Italian city-states and the decline of its maritime power due to the silting of its harbor. The city experienced periods of political instability and was eventually conquered by Florence in the 15th century, leading to its incorporation into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany.

  • Modern Era: Pisa became part of the Kingdom of Italy in 1861, following the Italian unification process. In the modern era, the city has become renowned for its rich history, architectural wonders, and its status as a hub for education and research, primarily due to the presence of the prestigious University of Pisa and other research institutions.

Today, Pisa is a popular tourist destination known for its iconic landmarks, historical significance, and vibrant cultural scene, attracting visitors from around the world who come to explore its architectural marvels and experience the charm of this ancient Italian city.

Experiences

Pisa, a city in the Tuscany region of Italy, offers visitors a rich cultural experience with a variety of attractions and activities to explore. Here are some of the top things to do in Pisa:

  1. Leaning Tower of Pisa (Torre Pendente): Visit the iconic Leaning Tower of Pisa, one of Italy's most famous landmarks, and climb to the top for a breathtaking panoramic view of the city.

  2. Piazza dei Miracoli (Square of Miracles): Explore the Piazza dei Miracoli, a UNESCO World Heritage site, which houses the Leaning Tower, the Cathedral (Duomo), the Baptistry, and the Camposanto Monumentale (monumental cemetery).

  3. Pisa Cathedral (Duomo di Pisa): Admire the stunning architecture of the Pisa Cathedral, a masterpiece of Romanesque design, known for its intricate facade and beautiful interior.

  4. Pisa Baptistry (Battistero): Visit the Pisa Baptistry, an architectural marvel renowned for its acoustics and exquisite design, located adjacent to the Cathedral.

  5. Pisa Botanical Gardens (Orto Botanico): Take a leisurely stroll through the Pisa Botanical Gardens, one of the oldest botanical gardens in Europe, featuring a diverse collection of plant species and a peaceful atmosphere.

  6. Piazza dei Cavalieri: Explore the historic Piazza dei Cavalieri, once the political center of medieval Pisa, and admire the impressive architecture of the Palazzo della Carovana and the Church of Santo Stefano dei Cavalieri.

  7. Museo dell'Opera del Duomo: Visit the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo to view a collection of artworks, sculptures, and historical artifacts related to the Piazza dei Miracoli complex.

  8. River Arno and Bridges: Enjoy a leisurely walk along the banks of the River Arno and cross the various bridges, such as Ponte di Mezzo and Ponte Solferino, to enjoy picturesque views of the city.

  9. University of Pisa: Explore the historic buildings of the University of Pisa, one of the oldest universities in Italy, known for its academic excellence and vibrant student life.

  10. Local Cuisine and Shopping: Indulge in authentic Tuscan cuisine at local restaurants and trattorias, and explore the city's shops and markets to experience the local culture and cuisine.

Pisa offers a blend of historical landmarks, cultural experiences, and culinary delights, making it a captivating destination for travelers seeking to immerse themselves in the rich heritage of Italy.

Pistoia

A Brief History

Pistoia is a charming city located in the Tuscany region of Italy. Its history dates back to ancient times, with evidence of settlements as early as the 2nd millennium BCE. The city has a rich historical and cultural background, which has contributed to its significance in the region.

During the Roman era, Pistoia was known as Pistoria and served as a significant hub for trade and commerce. After the fall of the Roman Empire, the city faced periods of political instability and underwent various changes in ruling powers, including domination by the Lombards and the Franks.

Pistoia flourished during the Middle Ages, becoming a free commune in the 12th century. The city witnessed periods of prosperity, as evidenced by the construction of notable religious and civic buildings, such as the Pistoia Cathedral and the Palazzo dei Vescovi.

In the following centuries, Pistoia faced turbulent times, including conflicts with other powerful city-states in the region. The city later came under the influence of powerful families, including the Medici, as Tuscany became part of the Grand Duchy of Tuscany.

During the Renaissance, Pistoia continued to thrive culturally and economically, contributing significantly to the arts and architecture of the period. The city's historical center still retains much of its medieval and Renaissance charm, with well-preserved architecture and landmarks.

In more recent history, Pistoia played a role in the Italian unification movement of the 19th century, contributing to the efforts that led to the establishment of the Kingdom of Italy in 1861.

Today, Pistoia is known for its well-preserved medieval and Renaissance architecture, its vibrant cultural scene, and its rich heritage in arts and crafts. The city attracts visitors from around the world who come to explore its historical landmarks, picturesque squares, and vibrant local culture.

Experiences

Pistoia offers a variety of attractions and activities for visitors to enjoy, reflecting its rich cultural heritage and natural beauty. Here are some things you can do in Pistoia:

  1. Explore the Historic Center: Take a leisurely stroll through the historic center to admire the well-preserved medieval and Renaissance architecture. Don't miss landmarks such as the Pistoia Cathedral, the Baptistry, and the Ospedale del Ceppo, known for its unique Renaissance façade.

  2. Visit Museums and Galleries: Discover the city's art and history through its various museums and galleries. The Marino Marini Museum, the Museo Civico, and the Museo del Tessuto (Textile Museum) are just a few places where you can delve into Pistoia's cultural heritage.

  3. Enjoy the Local Cuisine: Indulge in the authentic flavors of Tuscany by trying local specialties such as ribollita (a traditional Tuscan soup), Pistoia's renowned cured meats, and delicious wines from the region. Visit local restaurants and trattorias to savor the authentic Tuscan culinary experience.

  4. Relax in the Green Spaces: Take a break from the city's hustle and bustle by visiting one of Pistoia's beautiful parks, such as the Oasi Naturale del Ginepraio or the Giardino Zoologico di Pistoia (Pistoia Zoo), which is known for its conservation efforts and diverse animal species.

  5. Attend Cultural Events: Check the local events calendar for various cultural events, including art exhibitions, music festivals, and traditional celebrations. Pistoia hosts several events throughout the year, offering visitors an opportunity to immerse themselves in the city's vibrant cultural scene.

  6. Shop at Local Markets: Explore the local markets, such as the daily market in Piazza della Sala, to shop for fresh produce, local goods, and artisanal products. Engage with local vendors and experience the authentic market culture of Pistoia.

  7. Day Trips to Nearby Attractions: Take day trips to nearby attractions such as the Tuscan countryside, the Montalbano Hills, or the nearby cities of Florence, Lucca, and Pisa, which are easily accessible from Pistoia.

With its rich history, cultural offerings, and picturesque landscapes, Pistoia provides a delightful experience for travelers seeking an authentic taste of Tuscany.

Siena

A Brief History

Siena, located in the heart of Tuscany, Italy, has a rich history dating back to ancient times. Here is a brief overview of its history:

  • Ancient origins: Siena was originally an Etruscan settlement and later became a Roman colony known as Sena Julia during the Roman Republic.

  • Medieval era: During the Middle Ages, Siena flourished as a city-state and emerged as a major economic and cultural center in Tuscany. The city experienced a period of significant growth and prosperity, contributing to the development of its distinctive Gothic architecture and artistic heritage.

  • Rivalry with Florence: Siena was a key rival of Florence during the medieval period, with both cities competing for power and influence in Tuscany. The rivalry between Siena and Florence culminated in the famous Battle of Montaperti in 1260, where the Sienese were initially victorious over the Florentines.

  • Renaissance period: Despite its rivalry with Florence, Siena experienced a period of artistic and cultural growth during the Renaissance. The city produced renowned artists, scholars, and architects, contributing to the flourishing of the arts and humanistic thought in Tuscany.

  • Incorporation into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany: Siena was later incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in the 16th century, becoming a part of the broader territory ruled by the Medici family. Siena remained under Florentine and later Tuscan rule until the unification of Italy in the 19th century.

Today, Siena is renowned for its well-preserved medieval cityscape, including its historic center, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city continues to attract visitors from around the world who come to admire its architectural treasures, cultural heritage, and annual events, such as the Palio di Siena, a renowned horse race that takes place twice a year in the city's central square, the Piazza del Campo.

Experiences

Siena offers a variety of attractions and activities for visitors to enjoy. Here are some of the top things to do in Siena:

  1. Explore the historic city center: Take a stroll through the city's well-preserved medieval streets and visit the Piazza del Campo, one of Europe's greatest medieval squares and the site of the famous Palio horse race.

  2. Visit the Siena Cathedral (Duomo di Siena): Admire the stunning Gothic architecture of the Siena Cathedral, known for its intricate facade, impressive interior, and the breathtaking Piccolomini Library, which houses rare illuminated manuscripts and frescoes.

  3. Discover the Palazzo Pubblico: Explore the Palazzo Pubblico, the historic city hall of Siena, which houses the Civic Museum (Museo Civico) and features notable artworks, including the famous frescoes in the Hall of the Nine (Sala della Pace) by Ambrogio Lorenzetti.

  4. Attend the Palio di Siena: If you're visiting during the summer, witness the thrilling Palio di Siena, a traditional horse race that takes place in the Piazza del Campo, attracting both locals and visitors from around the world.

  5. Enjoy local cuisine: Indulge in traditional Tuscan cuisine at the local trattorias and restaurants, where you can savor dishes such as pici pasta, ribollita, and bistecca alla fiorentina, paired with local wines, including Chianti and Vernaccia di San Gimignano.

  6. Visit museums and art galleries: Explore the city's rich artistic heritage by visiting museums and art galleries, such as the Pinacoteca Nazionale, which houses a significant collection of Sienese paintings, and the Museo dell'Opera Metropolitana, featuring sculptures and artworks from the Siena Cathedral.

  7. Take a day trip to the surrounding countryside: Explore the picturesque Tuscan countryside surrounding Siena, with its rolling hills, vineyards, and olive groves. Visit nearby towns and villages, such as San Gimignano and Montalcino, known for their cultural significance and scenic beauty.

These activities provide just a glimpse of the diverse cultural, historical, and culinary experiences that Siena has to offer, making it an ideal destination for travelers interested in exploring the rich heritage and natural beauty of Tuscany.

pages.title: Countryside Festivals & Entertainments
pages.mainHtml:
Countryside Festivals & Entertainments

Tuscany hosts a vibrant array of popular festivals around the world, local countryside celebrations/festivals, and entertainments, reflecting the region's rich cultural heritage.

Here's a glimpse of some of the festivals and events:

Palio di Siena: This historic horse race in Siena takes place twice a year, attracting locals and tourists alike. The city comes alive with pageantry, parades, and intense horse races around the iconic Piazza del Campo.

Puccini Festival: Held in Torre del Lago, this festival celebrates the works of composer Giacomo Puccini. Performances of his famous operas take place in an open-air theater near Lake Massaciuccoli, creating a magical setting.

Chianti Classico Wine Festival: Wine enthusiasts flock to Greve in Chianti for this festival, celebrating the renowned Chianti Classico wines. It includes wine tastings, local food, and cultural events.

Volterra AD 1398: History comes to life in Volterra with this medieval festival. The town transforms into a medieval setting with costumed processions, markets, and historical reenactments.

Giostra del Saracino (Joust of the Saracen): Arezzo hosts this medieval jousting tournament, where knights compete in an exciting display of skill and horsemanship, dressed in elaborate period costumes.

Cortonantiquaria: Antique enthusiasts gather in Cortona for this fair, featuring a diverse collection of antiques, art, and vintage items.

The "Sagra del Tartufo" is a festive event that celebrates the prized truffle in Tuscany. One of the places where this festival takes place is San Miniato, renowned for the quality of white truffles. During the event, visitors have the opportunity to taste delicious truffle-based dishes, participate in culinary events, and explore local markets offering a variety of truffle products.

The "Sagra della Polenta" is a festive event that celebrates polenta in Italy. This traditional festival often takes place in various regions, each putting its unique twist on the celebration. During the event, communities come together to enjoy and showcase various preparations of polenta, a popular Italian dish made from boiled cornmeal.

Entertainment in Tuscany is not limited to festivals; the region also offers a dynamic arts scene with theaters, galleries, and street performances. From classical concerts to contemporary art exhibitions, Tuscany provides a cultural feast for residents and visitors alike year around. There are so many festivals and events to come and see year around.

pages.title: Jewelry
pages.mainHtml:
Jewelry

In Tuscany, jewelry reflects a blend of tradition, craftsmanship, and contemporary design. The region has a rich history of goldsmithing and jewelry-making, and you can find a diverse range of styles that cater to various tastes.

In Tuscany, jewelry reflects a blend of tradition, craftsmanship, and contemporary design. The region has a rich history of goldsmithing and jewelry-making, and you can find a diverse range of styles that cater to various tastes. Here are some characteristics of jewelry in Tuscany:

  1. Goldsmithing Tradition: Tuscany, particularly Florence, has a longstanding tradition of goldsmithing dating back to the Renaissance. This heritage is evident in the intricate craftsmanship and attention to detail in many Tuscan jewelry pieces.

  2. Artisanal Craftsmanship: Artisanal jewelry-making is highly valued in Tuscany. Many jewelers in the region pride themselves on creating unique, handcrafted pieces. You can find a variety of artisan workshops producing bespoke items.

  3. Symbolism and History: Tuscan jewelry often incorporates symbols and designs inspired by the region's rich history and cultural heritage. Elements from the Renaissance, Etruscan art, and medieval times may influence the designs.

  4. Contemporary Designs: While honoring tradition, Tuscany's jewelry scene is not stuck in the past. Many designers in the region create contemporary and modern pieces, combining innovation with the timeless elegance of traditional craftsmanship.

  5. Local Gemstones: Tuscan jewelry may feature locally sourced gemstones. For example, the region is known for its beautiful coral, which is often used in crafting unique and distinctive pieces.

  6. Elegance and Simplicity: Tuscan jewelry often embraces a sense of elegance and simplicity. Whether it's a classic gold piece or a modern design, there's a timeless quality to Tuscan jewelry that appeals to a wide audience.

  7. Markets and Boutiques: Tuscany boasts vibrant markets and boutique shops where you can explore and purchase jewelry. Florence, in particular, is known for its jewelry stores, ranging from traditional establishments to contemporary boutiques.

  8. Whether you're interested in classic gold pieces, artisanal creations, or modern designs, Tuscany offers a diverse and enchanting array of jewelry that captures the essence of its cultural and artistic heritage.

Olive oil tasting in Tuscany is a delightful experience, revealing the region's renowned fruity and robust flavors. Tuscan olive oils are celebrated for their well-balanced profiles, offering a sensory journey that reflects the rich agricultural traditions of the region.

Within 45 days of receipt of the appeal, we will inform you in writing of any action taken or not taken in response to the appeal, including a written explanation of the reasons for the decisions. If the appeal is denied, you may contact the Attorney General to submit a complaint.

We do not charge a fee to respond to your request, for up to one request per year.

sections.heading: Further information about retention time
sections.html:
Unless specified otherwise in this document, Personal Data shall be processed and stored for as long as required by the purpose they have been collected for and may be retained for longer due to applicable legal obligation or based on the Users’ consent.

Therefore:

  • Personal Data collected for purposes related to the performance of a contract between the Owner and the User shall be retained until such contract has been fully performed.

  • Personal Data collected for the purposes of the Owner’s legitimate interests shall be retained as long as needed to fulfill such purposes. Users may find specific information regarding the legitimate interests pursued by the Owner within the relevant sections of this document or by contacting the Owner.

The Owner may be allowed to retain Personal Data for a longer period whenever the User has given consent to such processing, as long as such consent is not withdrawn. Furthermore, the Owner may be obliged to retain Personal Data for a longer period whenever required to fulfil a legal obligation or upon order of an authority.

Once the retention period expires, Personal Data shall be deleted. Therefore, the right of access, the right to erasure, the right to rectification and the right to data portability cannot be enforced after expiration of the retention period.

sections.heading: The rights of Users based on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
sections.html:
Users may exercise certain rights regarding their Data processed by the Owner.

In particular, Users have the right to do the following, to the extent permitted by law:

  • Withdraw their consent at any time. Users have the right to withdraw consent where they have previously given their consent to the processing of their Personal Data.

  • Object to processing of their Data. Users have the right to object to the processing of their Data if the processing is carried out on a legal basis other than consent.

  • Access their Data. Users have the right to learn if Data is being processed by the Owner, obtain disclosure regarding certain aspects of the processing and obtain a copy of the Data undergoing processing.

  • Verify and seek rectification. Users have the right to verify the accuracy of their Data and ask for it to be updated or corrected.

  • Restrict the processing of their Data. Users have the right to restrict the processing of their Data. In this case, the Owner will not process their Data for any purpose other than storing it.

  • Have their Personal Data deleted or otherwise removed.Users have the right to obtain the erasure of their Data from the Owner.

  • Receive their Data and have it transferred to another controller. Users have the right to receive their Data in a structured, commonly used and machine readable format and, if technically feasible, to have it transmitted to another controller without any hindrance.

  • Lodge a complaint. Users have the right to bring a claim before their competent data protection authority.

Users are also entitled to learn about the legal basis for Data transfers abroad including to any international organization governed by public international law or set up by two or more countries, such as the UN, and about the security measures taken by the Owner to safeguard their Data.

sections.heading: Categories of personal information collected, used, sold, or shared
sections.html:
In this section we summarize the categories of personal information that we've collected, used, sold, or shared and the purposes thereof. You can read about these activities in detail in the section titled “Detailed information on the processing of Personal Data” within this document.

We have collected the following categories of personal information about you: identifiers, commercial information and internet or other electronic network activity information.

We have collected the following categories of sensitive personal information: payment info

We will not collect additional categories of personal information without notifying you.

You have the right to request that we limit the use or disclosure of your sensitive personal information to only that which is necessary to perform the services or provide the goods, as is reasonably expected by an average consumer.

We can also use your sensitive personal information to perform specific purposes set forth by the law (such as, including but not limited to, helping to ensure security and integrity; undertaking activities to verify or maintain the quality or safety of our service) and as authorized by the relevant regulations.

Outside of the aforementioned specific purposes, you have the right to freely request, at any time, that we do not use or disclose your sensitive personal information. This means that whenever you ask us to stop using your sensitive personal information, we will abide by your request and we will instruct our service providers and contractors to do the same.

To fully exercise your right to limit the use or disclosure of your sensitive personal information you can contact us at any time, using the contact details provided in this document.

For a simplified method you can also use the privacy choices link provided on www.supertuscany.org.

We use any personal information collected from you in connection with the submission of your request solely for the purposes of complying with the request.

Once you have exercised this right, we are required to wait at least 12 months before asking whether you have changed your mind.

We may use your personal information to allow the operational functioning of www.supertuscany.org and features thereof (“business purposes”). In such cases, your personal information will be processed in a fashion necessary and proportionate to the business purpose for which it was collected, and strictly within the limits of compatible operational purposes.

We may also use your personal information for other reasons such as for commercial purposes (as indicated within the section “Detailed information on the processing of Personal Data” within this document), as well as for complying with the law and defending our rights before the competent authorities where our rights and interests are threatened or we suffer an actual damage.

We won’t process your information for unexpected purposes, or for purposes incompatible with the purposes originally disclosed, without your consent.

Unless stated otherwise inside the “Detailed information on the processing of Personal Data” section, we will not retain your personal information for longer than is reasonably necessary for the purpose(s) they have been collected for.

We collect the above-mentioned categories of personal information, either directly or indirectly, from you when you use www.supertuscany.org.

For example, you directly provide your personal information when you submit requests via any forms on www.supertuscany.org. You also provide personal information indirectly when you navigate www.supertuscany.org, as personal information about you is automatically observed and collected.

Finally, we may collect your personal information from third parties that work with us in connection with the Service or with the functioning of this Application and features thereof.

For our purposes, the word “third party” means a person who is not any of the following: a service provider or a contractor, as defined by the CCPA.

We disclose your personal information with the third parties listed in detail in the section titled “Detailed information on the processing of Personal Data” within this document. These third parties are grouped and categorized in accordance with the different purposes of processing.

For our purposes, the word “sale” means any “selling, renting, releasing, disclosing, disseminating, making available, transferring or otherwise communicating orally, in writing, or by electronic means, a consumer's personal information by the business to a third party, for monetary or other valuable consideration”, as defined by the CCPA.

This means that, for example, a sale can happen whenever an application runs ads, or makes statistical analyses on the traffic or views, or simply because it uses tools such as social network plugins and the like.

For our purposes, the word “sharing” means any “sharing, renting, releasing, disclosing, disseminating, making available, transferring, or otherwise communicating orally, in writing, or by electronic or other means, a consumer's personal information by the business to a third party for cross-context behavioral advertising, whether or not for monetary or other valuable consideration, including transactions between a business and a third party for cross-context behavioral advertising for the benefit of a business in which no money is exchanged”, as defined by the CCPA.
Please note that the exchange of personal information with a service provider pursuant to a written contract that meets the requirements set by the CCPA, does not constitute a sale or sharing of your personal information.

We sell or share your personal information with the third parties listed in detail in the section titled “Detailed information on the processing of Personal Data” within this document. These third parties are grouped and categorized in accordance with the different purposes of processing.

You have the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information. This means that whenever you request us to stop selling or sharing your personal information, we will abide by your request.
Such requests can be made freely, at any time, without submitting any verifiable request.
To fully exercise your right to opt out, you can contact us at any time using the contact details provided in this document.
For a simplified opt-out method you can also use the privacy choices link provided on www.supertuscany.org.

If you want to submit requests to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information via a user-enabled global privacy control, like the Global Privacy Control (“GPC”), you are free to do so and we will abide by such request in a frictionless manner (as defined in the CPRA regulations). The GPC consists of a setting or extension in the browser or mobile device and acts as a mechanism that websites can use to indicate they support the GPC signal. If you want to use GPC, you can download and enable it via a participating browser or browser extension. More information about downloading GPC is available here.

We use any personal information collected from you in connection with the submission of your opt-out request solely for the purposes of complying with the opt-out request.

Once you have opted out, we are required to wait at least 12 months before asking whether you have changed your mind.

sections.heading: The right to access personal information: the right to know and to portability

  • the sources from which the personal information is collected;

  • the purposes for which we use your information;

  • to whom we disclose such information;

  • the specific pieces of personal information we have collected about you.

You also have the right to know what personal information is sold or shared and to whom. In particular, you have the right to request two separate lists from us where we disclose:

  • the categories of personal information that we sold or shared about you and the categories of third parties to whom the personal information was sold or shared;

  • the categories of personal information that we disclosed about you for a business purpose and the categories of persons to whom it was disclosed for a business purpose.

The disclosure described above will be limited to the personal information collected or used over the past 12 months.

If we deliver our response electronically, the information enclosed will be "portable", i.e. delivered in an easily usable format to enable you to transmit the information to another entity without hindrance — provided that this is technically feasible.

sections.html:
To exercise the rights described above, you need to submit your verifiable request to us by contacting us via the details provided in this document.

For us to respond to your request, it’s necessary that we know who you are. Therefore, you can only exercise the above rights by making a verifiable request which must:

  • provide sufficient information that allows us to reasonably verify you are the person about whom we collected personal information or an authorized representative;

  • describe your request with sufficient detail that allows us to properly understand, evaluate, and respond to it.

We will not respond to any request if we are unable to verify your identity and therefore confirm the personal information in our possession actually relates to you.

Making a verifiable consumer request does not require you to create an account with us. We will use any personal information collected from you in connection with the verification of your request solely for the purposes of verification and shall not further disclose the personal information, retain it longer than necessary for purposes of verification, or use it for unrelated purposes.

If you are an adult, you can make a verifiable request on behalf of a child under your parental authority.

You can submit a maximum number of 2 requests over a period of 12 months.

sections.html:
We will respond to your request without undue delay, but in all cases and at the latest within 45 days of its receipt. Should we need more time, we will explain to you the reasons why, and how much more time we need. In this regard, please note that we may take up to 90 days to fulfill your request.

If the appeal is denied you may contact the Attorney General to submit a complaint.

We do not charge a fee to respond to your request, for up to two requests per year.

  • access personal data. You have the right to request that we confirm whether or not we are processing your personal data. You also have the right to access such personal data.

  • request the deletion of your personal data. You have the right to request that we delete any of your personal data.

  • obtain a copy of your personal data. We will provide your personal data in a portable and usable format that allows you to transfer data easily to another entity – provided that this is technically feasible.

  • opt out of the processing of your personal data for the purposes of targeted advertising or the sale of personal data.

In any case, we will not increase the cost of, or decrease the availability of, a product or service, based solely on the exercise of any of your rights and unrelated to the feasibility or the value of a service. However, to the extent permitted by the law, we may offer a different price, rate, level, quality, or selection of goods or services to you, including offering goods or services for no fee, if our offer is related to your voluntary participation in a bona fide loyalty, rewards, premium features, discounts, or club card program.

sections.heading: How to exercise your rights
sections.html:
To exercise the rights described above, you need to submit your request to us by contacting us via the contact details provided in this document.

For us to respond to your request, we need to know who you are and which right you wish to exercise.

We will not respond to any request if we are unable to verify your identity using commercially reasonable efforts and therefore confirm that the personal data in our possession actually relate to you. In such cases, we may request that you provide additional information which is reasonably necessary to authenticate you and your request. We may retain your email address to respond to your request.

If you are an adult, you can make a request on behalf of a child under your parental authority.

sections.heading: How and when we are expected to handle your request
sections.html:
We will respond to your request without undue delay, but in all cases and at the latest within 45 days of its receipt. Should we need more time, we will explain to you the reasons why, and how much more time we need. In this regard, please note that we may take up to 90 days to fulfill your request.

Should we deny your request, we will explain to you the reasons behind our denial without undue delay, but in all cases and at the latest within 45 days of receipt of the request.

We do not charge a fee to respond to your request, for up to one request per year.

Property Description

Palazzo Rosadi is a luxurious Tuscan villa at only 3 km from Monterchi, where Piero della Francesca painted one of his most famous frescoes “La Madonna del Parto” towards the end of the 1500s. It is consequently an ideal setting for reaching small characteristic villages in Umbria, the splendid Tuscan art cities like Cortona and Arezzo.

The Palazzo dates back to 1785 and on the inside one can breath the antique atmosphere as though time has stopped. Then the Palazzo was enlarged and the bedrooms and lounge rooms were decorated by a famous local artist, Luigi Puletti, a precursor of Liberty style. The villa, with private swimming pool is surrounded by 25 hectares of land with century old oaks, cypresses and pine trees through which a natural park has been created, so that the guests can admire the flora and fauna typical of this area of Tuscany.

A one hectare rose garden surrounds the villa and on one side there is the pergola with moscatello and canaiola grapes used for the production of holy wine. The swimming pool (6 mt by 12 mt and 1.5 mt deep and which has a magnificent panoramic view) is located on an lower level with respect to the villa and is complete with umbrellas, gazebo with table, chairs, sunbeds in aluminium and a shower. The garden and the swimming pool are lit up at night, ideal for spending summer evenings, perhaps tasting a good glass of local wine. Palazzo Rosadi represents the perfect union of tradition and modernity, where you will be spoiled by the attention of the owner, who will do everything possible to make your holiday unique. On request you can enjoy the external jacuzzi. The villa has wifi.

All of the bedroom have AC and ensuite bathrooms. Ground Floor Loungeroom with armchairs, dining table and chairs for 12 people, TV satellite, stereo, large fireplace (not functional).
